Question
========
Conduct a t-test to see whether life satisfaction depends upon the type of pet a person has. Use the Welch version of the t-test, for more robustness against possible unequal variances. What is the calculated t-value? Round to two decimal places.

t-value: ##ANSWER1##

Degrees of freedom: ##ANSWER2##

Answerlist
----------
* 
* 

Solution
========
On average, the life satisfaction of cat owners (M = 60.13, SE = 3.93) was significantly higher than that of people who had fish as pets (M = 38.17, SE = 4.48), t(17.84) = -3.69, p = 0.002, d = -1.63 [-2.65, -0.57]. Note that I report the results of the Welch version of the t-test, as recommended in the book, to have more robustness against possible unequal variances.

(With the groups the other way around, t = 3.69; that counts as correct too.)

DSUJ §9.8, p. 380. discoverjasp: [Task 9.5](https://discoverjasp.com/pages/smart_alex.html#task-9.5), [results](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_alex/alex_09_05-06.html).
